beats.narration_text: Hallo — this is Liam, in for Komal. You used to type what you saw. Now a photo can be the query. Today: what AI image search actually is, how the same machine moved through luxury, conservation, and circular resale, and one catalog already matching individuals from a snapshot.

beats.narration_text: Here is the whole idea. AI image search is not a smarter caption. It is a query that looks — you show an image, and the system retrieves neighbors from an index.

beats.narration_text: Start with names. A caption describes a photo. A classifier labels it: bag, zebra, sneaker. Image search is different: it retrieves. Ranked matches from a catalog. Those are not synonyms.

beats.narration_text: Why this is live now. Visual embeddings let a photo sit next to other photos. Google Lens, announced in twenty seventeen, made the camera a search box. Luxury marketplaces pointed it at a street look. Conservation pointed it at a fluke. Same retrieval. Different indexes.

beats.narration_text: What it changed. Luxury: Farfetch shipped visual search in twenty eighteen — snap a look, retrieve similar S.K.U.s. Conservation: find this animal again by its markings. Animal welfare: a lost-pet photo is the same query against found listings. Circular resale: Posh Lens, twenty twenty-three — find a second-hand match instead of a new one. If a street photo can retrieve the S.K.U., the closed door is a catalog.

beats.narration_text: Worked example. Wildbook. Upload a photo of a whale, a zebra, a dolphin. The system finds the animal in the frame, then searches a catalog of individuals by natural markings, and returns ranked matches. It does not decide for you. A researcher confirms. That is image search: a photo as a query against an index of lives. Not S.K.U.s.

beats.narration_text: Let's recap with Claude. A caption describes. A classifier labels. Search retrieves. Luxury, conservation, resale, and lost-pet matching run the same query. Design judgment: if it cannot retrieve neighbors, it is not image search. Ask what a false match would cost.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude with a photo from a field you actually know — a lookbook, a camera-trap, a resale listing, a lost-pet poster. (1) Caption, label, or search — which machine is running? (2) What index would the neighbors come from? (3) What would a false match cost in that field? Score the system: retrieving, or just naming. Run it before the next visual-search meeting.
